title: AuroraCloud + Redwood Reference Architecture Tech Sync

Deployment options: hosted vs private/VPC vs on-prem

next_steps: Redwood to share updated reference architecture doc and CloudFormation templates (Alex) - target 2026-11-05
Aurora to provide sample tenant VPC network topology and IAM constraints (Evan) - target 2026-11-03
Schedule joint benchmarking window for 2 hours of perf runs (Priya + Daniel) - propose slots by 2026-11-02
Exchange legal/marketplace onboarding checklist (Alex to loop in partnerships)
action_items: Alex Kim: Upload ref-arch v1 PDF and CF templates to shared drive (/drive/redwood/aurora/ref-arch-v1.pdf) - due 2026-11-05
Priya Shah: Prepare test harness and perf checklist for benchmarking - due 2026-11-02
Evan Park: Share AuroraCloud marketplace onboarding checklist and sample terms - due 2026-11-03

meeting_header:
Date: 2026-10-29 | Time: 10:00am - 10:58am PT | Duration: 58m
Location: Zoom | Recording: enabled
Attendees: Alex Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Marco Ruiz (Redwood SE), Evan Park (Aurora PM), Sofia Martínez (Aurora Solutions Architect), Daniel Zhou (Aurora Eng Lead), Lena Fischer (Aurora Cloud Ops)
transcript:
[00:00] Alex Kim: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I think we have about 58 minutes on the calendar. Quick roll call?
[00:08] Evan Park: Hey Alex, Evan here, Sofia and Dan are with me, Lena's on for networking questions.
[00:14] Priya Shah: Priya from Redwood, Marco too, we'll jump into the arch diagram and the CF artifacts.
[00:22] Sofia Martínez: Sounds good.
[00:28] Alex Kim: Ok high level goals for today: finalize reference architecture for the Aurora marketplace listing, agree on what we need for the public listing (artifacts, screenshots, pricing guidance), and align on private/VPC deployment constraints including KMS, IAM, and audit logs.
[00:48] Marco Ruiz: We'll also want to confirm the inference runtime shape and the quantization profile we recommend for your SKU listings.
[00:55] Daniel Zhou: Quick note — our ops folks care about how data is handled in Dedicated vs Private — like is user data ever seen by Redwood in marketplace flow?
[01:05] Alex Kim: Great question. For the marketplace public listing we can support both hosted and marketplace-connected dedicated models. By default hosted API does not store customer data beyond transient logs, but for enterprise listings customers will typically choose Dedicated or Private with VPC peering so no cross-tenant data exposure.
[01:30] Lena Fischer: On VPC peering, we need to ensure support for our transit gateway topology; do you support direct ENI attachment or only NAT?
[01:40] Priya Shah: We can do either depending on the private deployment. Our Private offering supports customer-managed VPC with ENI attachments; there's also an option for SSM/agent-based connectivity in air-gapped setups. We'll share the network appendix.
[01:57] Sofia Martínez: KMS — we need BYOK with HSM-backed keys. Are you compatible with Aurora's keywrap?
[02:06] Marco Ruiz: Yes, Redwood Private integrates with customer KMS/HSM via standard KMIP or cloud KMS APIs; we have a keywrap flow documented. Some of the naming got munged in older docs — we'll send the updated sequence.
[02:25] Alex Kim: Moving to the marketplace listing checklist — items we need: short product description, supported deployment modes, reference arch diagram, estimated per-invocation tpm or token cost, sample benchmark numbers, SSO/SAML instructions, and compliance badges (SOC2/ISO).
[02:45] Evan Park: For pricing guidance on the marketplace, do you have suggested SKU tiers? We prefer simple tiers: dev, standard, enterprise.
[02:52] Alex Kim: We can propose three tiers — dev (hosted, shared capacity), reserved (dedicated capacity), private (VPC/on-prem). We'll include guidance on expected token throughput and recommended GPU shapes per tier.
[03:10] Daniel Zhou: For the ref arch diagram, can you annotate where the KV cache lives and how caching works across pods?
[03:18] Priya Shah: Yes, in our runtime the KV cache sits on the serving nodes; in Dedicated it's local to the GPU pool, in Private we can configure a shared Redis-backed prefix cache if you want cross-node reuse. Note — shared cache has tradeoffs for cold-start isolation.
[03:40] Sofia Martínez: That sounds reasonable. Do you support model pinning and can we control rollouts per tenant?
[03:46] Marco Ruiz: Absolutely, rollout policies are configurable — canary, A/B, percent-based. We'll call out the control-plane hooks in the ref arch.
[03:55] Alex Kim: There's a doc I'm sharing in chat: /drive/redwood/aurora/ref-arch-v1.pdf — that's the draft. We'll iterate.
[04:05] Evan Park: I see it. Quick scan says the network path shows NAT — we'll need an ENI variant for our prod customers.
[04:14] Priya Shah: Noted.
[04:16] Alex Kim: On compliance — we can surface SOC2 Type II and ISO certs in the marketplace listing. For deeper audits we can offer audit logs and per-token tracing.
[04:30] Lena Fischer: For audit logs, can we ship to our Splunk/S3 bucket?
[04:36] Marco Ruiz: Yes, audit logs can be forwarded to customer S3 or to SIEMs via webhook. Data residency options are included.
[04:44] Daniel Zhou: Regarding the CF/Terraform artifacts — are they opinionated or do we provide modules?
[04:50] Priya Shah: We provide Terraform modules and CloudFormation templates for the common patterns — VPC peering, ENI setup, IAM roles and KMS policies. The modules are parameterized for region and instance shapes.
[05:05] Alex Kim: Let's walk through the draft ref arch (screen share).
[05:10] [screen share starts, brief pause]
[05:24] Priya Shah: Slide 1 shows the Marketplace flow: Aurora customer clicks listing -> provisioning flow calls Redwood Marketplace API -> creates dedicated capacity pool or attaches Private agent depending on selection. We note the provisioning timeline typically 10-20 minutes for dedicated pools.
[05:45] Sofia Martínez: 10-20 minutes — that's ok. For larger bookings is there a longer lead time?
[05:51] Marco Ruiz: Reserved capacity contracts can be scheduled with longer provisioning windows; we'll annotate lead times by GPU type.
[06:00] Alex Kim: Slide 3 shows the Private deployment options: VPC peering, ENI attach, and on-prem agent. The path with ENI keeps traffic within your VPC, so it's preferred for strict egress policies.
[06:18] Lena Fischer: One concern: how do you handle outbound updates and patches in air-gapped on-prem?
[06:24] Priya Shah: For air-gapped we provide an offline bundle and a signed update mechanism. It does require a scheduled maintenance window and pre-approval.
[06:36] Evan Park: Ok, any blockers on the CF artifacts?
[06:40] Alex Kim: The biggest unknown is naming conventions for Aurora IAM roles and some network CIDR choices. We'll need a sample from you.
[06:52] Daniel Zhou: We'll export our tenant VPC template.
[06:54] Alex Kim: Great.
[07:00] [07:00 - 15:00 condensed notes omitted for brevity in the transcript export, but present in recording]
[15:08] Priya Shah: Picking back up — benchmarking plan: we propose a 2 hour window where Redwood runs standard perf harness with your representative model (we recommend a 4k context LLM for Aurora use-case). We'll produce a spreadsheet with per-token latency p50/p95/p99 and throughput at different batch sizes.
[15:33] Daniel Zhou: We will provide seq length distributions and QPS patterns. For internal SLAs we need p95 < 300ms for short completions (< 128 tokens).
[15:45] Priya Shah: We'll test for those targets. Note that p95 is sensitive to batching and concurrency; we can tune batch sizes to meet p95 without blowing up cost.
[16:00] Marco Ruiz: Also note quantization choices affect quality. We'll include recommended int8 quant profiles and quality regression thresholds.
[16:18] Sofia Martínez: About quality — will you run evals against our prompt set?
[16:22] Alex Kim: Yes, we'll run evals against a customer-supplied prompt set and surface model regressions. That will be part of the benchmark deliverable.
[16:30] Evan Park: On the marketplace listing page, what screenshots do you typically include?
[16:35] Alex Kim: Typical listing includes architecture diagram, sample API call/SDK snippet, latency/throughput snapshot, and a short blurb on security/compliance. We can provide templates.
[16:48] Daniel Zhou: Are there licensing considerations for the models if we host them?
[16:53] Marco Ruiz: We'll document model licensing per catalog entry. If Aurora wants to include a 3rd-party open model in the listing we'll link license terms.
[17:05] Lena Fischer: For monitoring/tracing, can we integrate with Aurora's existing APM?
[17:10] Priya Shah: Traces can be exported via OTLP to your APM, and we have per-request trace IDs you can correlate.
[17:18] Evan Park: Great.
[17:22] [brief cross talk]
[17:30] Alex Kim: Any regulatory concerns we should call out for the reference arch?
[17:35] Sofia Martínez: Data residency — some EU customers require data to not leave region. Also some gov customers require FIPS.
[17:44] Marco Ruiz: We can flag regional deployments and FIPS-compliant stacks in the doc.
[17:52] Daniel Zhou: For SSO, we use SAML and some customers need SCIM provisioning.
[17:58] Priya Shah: Supported. We'll include SAML + SCIM examples in the marketplace docs.
[18:06] Alex Kim: Ok let's talk tokenization and cost attribution — Aurora will want per-customer metering if listing through marketplace. How do you prefer to handle billing attribution?
[18:16] Marco Ruiz: We can surface per-tenant usage and either report usage to Aurora via marketplace hooks or invoice through Redwood with a revenue share. We'll align with partnership/legal.
[18:30] Evan Park: We'll need clear examples of how attribution looks in reports.
[18:35] Alex Kim: We'll include a sample CSV and dashboard screenshot.
[18:40] [20:00 - 40:00 sections omitted in transcript export but discuss deep config, CF parameters, edge cases like cold-starts and KV invalidation]
[40:12] Priya Shah: One tricky piece — KV cache invalidation when model variants are rolled out. We recommend tagging caches per-model-version to avoid cross-version contamination.
[40:26] Daniel Zhou: That will work. We'll also need an SLA for cache warm-up time for high-availability tenants.
[40:34] Marco Ruiz: We'll surface recommended warm-up strategies (scheduled warm-up jobs, preloading popular prefixes).
[40:50] Sofia Martínez: Are there any special networking ports or security groups required we need to include in our baseline templates?
[40:58] Priya Shah: We'll include a network appendix with security group ports, ENI policies, Route table entries, and recommended NACLs.
[41:10] Alex Kim: Wrapping toward the end — legal/marketplace onboarding: Redwood partnerships team will provide the marketplace onboarding checklist, logos, and co-marketing assets. Alex will loop in partnerships.
[41:26] Evan Park: Thanks. On marketing assets, can we co-brand the reference architecture diagram?
[41:31] Marco Ruiz: Yes, co-branding is ok per our partner handbook. We'll include a PNG and SVG.
[41:38] Alex Kim: Quick recap of action items and owners — I'll read them out.
[41:44] [Alex reads action items]
[42:10] Priya Shah: Scheduling the perf window — I'll send a Doodle today.
[42:16] Daniel Zhou: We'll fill sample seq distribution and upload to the shared drive.
[42:22] Sofia Martínez: And I'll validate the KMS flows with Lena.
[42:28] Evan Park: Ok good.
[42:34] Alex Kim: Any outstanding blockers?
[42:37] Lena Fischer: Nothing immediate. We'll need to review the CF templates for our naming conv.
[42:42] Alex Kim: Great. Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the doc and templates.
[42:49] [Meeting ends, recording continues a few seconds as people leave]
